title: Live price streaming
intro: Live prices reach the quote page through one global broadcast stream, but about 18 widgets each subscribe their own symbols and about 25 StreamBuilders each filter the stream again. Because a subscribe call replaces the whole subscription set, widgets that subscribe from build() keep undoing each other and re-sending the same symbols; nothing unsubscribes, depth keeps running after the user leaves, and ticks rebuild whole sections even when no value changed. These changes give the page one owner for its subscriptions, rebuild only the values that changed, and release what the page no longer shows, with safe per-widget first steps before the larger refactor.

changes.title: Add one tick hub per quote page
changes.summary: Today 18 StreamingBaseWidget states on the page each subscribe their own symbols, and about 25 StreamBuilders filter the one global quote stream. Add a QuoteTickHub owned by MoGetQuoteCubit. It subscribes the union of the page's symbols once, detects real value changes, samples at about 250 ms, and exposes one ValueListenable per symbol that widgets read with ValueListenableBuilder.
changes.risk_reason: Changes the subscription model of the whole quote page and how every live value reaches the UI. A wrong union drops prices for a section. Needs a feature flag (hub off = today's per-widget subscriptions) and a full regression pass during market hours.

Create the hub, register the page symbol(s) on load and asset switch, dispose it in close().
Add quote_tick_hub_enabled (default false).
First migrated widget (header price): ValueListenableBuilder on hub.listenable(symbol) when the flag is on.

changes.current: onTickReceived (trader_widgets StreamingBaseWidget.dart:54-59 and mosl_broadcaster streaming_base_widget.dart:85-88) is where(symbol).startWith(cache) on the single global PublishSubject. BroadcastChannelImpl.onBroadcast (broadcast_channel.dart:243-251) mutates the cached BroadcastResponse2 in place and publishes the same object again, and BroadcastResponse2 has no == override. So there is no change detection, .distinct() would block every later tick, and a ValueNotifier<BroadcastResponse2> never fires after the first value (see E4). TBT depth packets (QuoteEightyFour) are also published on the quote stream (packet_publisher.dart:60-65), so with 50-depth open every depth packet rebuilds every price widget of that symbol.

changes.summary: Six widgets call startQuoteStreaming on every build or parent update. Because subscribeQuote replaces the global subscription set, each call unsubscribes the other widgets' symbols and re-sends the full set. Move each call to initState, and to didUpdateWidget only when the symbol set actually changed. This is the safe first step before E1.
changes.risk_reason: Changes when subscribe packets are sent; if a symbol change is missed, a section stops updating. Each widget still subscribes its own symbols, so no shared code changes.

changes.title: Guard multicast switch on every subscribe
changes.summary: BroadCastHelper.startQuoteStreaming runs _switchToMulticastIfNeeded on every call. If multicast is enabled and the last connected URL is not a multicast URL, it stops and restarts the socket. That URL is cleared or overwritten on failover and mode change, so with today's frequent subscribe calls this can restart the socket repeatedly. Verify, then only attempt the switch once per connection.
changes.risk_reason: Shared socket code used by every module; a wrong guard could keep users on a non-multicast URL or stop the switch entirely.

files.change: Track _multicastSwitchAttemptedForConnection; skip while a switch is in progress or already tried since the last socket state change to loggedIn.

changes.current: isCurrentUrlMulticast is computed from urlStore.getLastConnectedUrl(). SocketCreator.updateSequence (mosl_socket_core socket_creator.dart:163-168) sets it to whatever URL actually logged in, clearLastConnectedUrl/resetLastUrlIfNeeded (170-190) remove it, and setConnectionMode can remove it (broadcast_helper.dart:123-129). When the multicast URL fails and a regular URL wins, or while the value is empty, every startQuoteStreaming call (E2: many per minute) runs stopStreaming() and startStreaming() again. Whether this happens in production depends on multiStreamBcast and which URL wins.
steps: Verify first: enable the broadcaster file log, open a quote page with multicast on, and count 'Stop Streaming' / 'Start Streaming' lines per minute.
If confirmed: add a flag that is set when a switch starts and cleared on the next socketStateStream loggedIn event; skip the switch while set.
Do not switch again after a multicast attempt has ended on a non-multicast URL in the same session (fallback was deliberate).
E1/E2 reduce the number of calls and therefore the exposure even before this lands.
safety: Keeps the TAR-I26178 behaviour for the first non-multicast connection.
Only removes repeated attempts; normal connect order (UrlStore.getConnectionUrls inserts multicast URLs first when isMultiCast) is unchanged.
regression_checks: Multicast-enabled user: connects to multicast; kill the multicast server: falls back once and stays connected.
Non-multicast user: no change.
Socket log shows no repeated Stop/Start Streaming while browsing a quote page.
changes.after_improvement: At most one multicast switch per connection instead of a possible stop/restart on every subscribe call.

changes.title: Ask BE about re-subscribe snapshots and idle ticks
changes.summary: The 465 KB/min idle traffic after market close needs a server-side answer: does the socket server send a full snapshot for every symbol in each subscribe packet, even if already subscribed, and does it send heartbeats or repeated unchanged ticks after the close? The answer decides how much E2/E1 alone will save.
changes.risk_reason: A question and a log capture; no code change in the app.
changes.be_request: For the quote broadcast socket (regular and TBT): (1) When a client sends a subscribe packet for symbols it is already subscribed to, does the server send a snapshot for each symbol again? (2) After market close, does the server send any packets per subscribed symbol (heartbeats, repeated last ticks, session packets), and at what rate? (3) Is there a packet size per QuoteOne/QuoteFour/QuoteEightyFour we can use to convert counts to KB? (4) Can the server ignore duplicate subscribes, or send snapshots only for newly added symbols?
changes.current: The client re-sends the full set whenever it differs from the last one (subscription.dart:67-82) and the page changes the set many times a minute (E2). BroadcastController also sends a NIFTY 50 snapshot as a ping when the socket has been silent for 50 s (broadcast_controller.dart:83-85, 370-377), which is small. Without the server answer we cannot tell whether 465 KB/min is snapshots, heartbeats or ticks.
steps: Capture: with the A7 probe on, log subscribe calls and symbols per call for 5 minutes after market close; capture bytes received on the broadcast socket in the same window (Android Studio network profiler or the broadcaster BroadcastStats log).
Send the capture with the questions to the socket team.
Feed the answer back into E1 (sampling) and E2 (expected saving).
safety: Information only; the follow-up sketch is not part of this item.
regression_checks: None for this item.
changes.after_improvement: A known split of idle traffic into snapshots, heartbeats and ticks, so the target of 10 KB/min or less can be planned with the right changes.
